questions.question: Which of the following architects designed the Gateway of India?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __**George Wittet.**__ 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Gateway of India**

 
 
• ​Gateway of India was built by the British government. It was designed by **George Wittet.**
 
• He was a Scottish Architect and was asked to design a Gateway to commemorate the visit of King George V and Queen Mary, before the Delhi Durbar, in December 1911.
 
• The Gateway of India** is located in**__ __Mumbai.__
 
• It was constructed in 1924.
 
• The main objective behind the construction of the Gateway of India was to commemorate the visit** of **King George V and Queen Mary to Bombay (Mumbai).
 
• In March 1911, Sir George Sydenham Clarke, who was then the Governor of Bombay, laid down the monument's foundation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Herbert Baker​​**

 
 
• Edwin Lutyens and Herbert Baker are two architects credited to have designed the city of New Delhi.
 
• Edwin Lutyens and Herbert Baker were both English architects and friends.
 
• New Delhi, after completion, was inaugurated in the year 1931 by Viceroy Lord Irwin.
 
• Rashtrapati Bhawan and Parliament was also designed by both these architects.
 
 
 
• **Henry Irwin****​**
 
 
• The Mysore Palace was once the **R****esidence of the Wodeyars**.
 
• Built in Indo-Saracenic style with domes, turrets, arches, and colonnades, the Palace is often compared with the **Buckingham Palace** of Britain because of its grandeur.
 
• **Henry Irwin, the British consultant architect of Madras state, designed it.
 
• The Golden Royal Elephant Throne, the Durbar Hall, and the Kalyan Mandap (wedding hall) are the main attractions in the palace.
 
• Walls leading to the Kalyan Mandap** are lined with intricate oil paintings, illustrating the royal procession of the **Mysore Dussehra Festival**.
 
 
 
• **Lauri Baker****​**
 
 
• Lawrence Wilfred **"Laurie" Baker **was a British-born Indian architect,.
 
• Renowned for his initiatives in cost-effective energy-efficient architecture and designs that maximized space, ventilation, and light and maintained an uncluttered yet striking aesthetic sensibility.
 
• He was the pioneer of sustainable architecture as well as organic architecture.
 
• He promoted the revival of regional building practices and the use of local materials.

questions.question: Who among the following sportspersons has been awarded the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award 2022?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __**Shri Sharath Kamal Achanta.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **Badminton pair Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty **have received the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award for the year 2023.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna**(Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award)**​**

 
 
• The **Khel Ratna Award**, officially known as the **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna** Award, was formerly known as the Rajiv Gandh**i Khel Ratna** Award in Sports and Games.
 
• It is the highest sporting honour in India.
 
• It is awarded annually by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports.
 
• The recipient(s)/are selected by a committee constituted by the Ministry and is honoured for their "spectacular and most outstanding performance in the field of sports over a period of four years" at the international level.
 
• As of 2020, the award comprises a medallion, a certificate, and a cash prize of ₹25 lakh 
 
• 
 
The cash prize was revised from ₹1 lakh to ₹3 lahks in 2000 to ₹5 lahks in 2002, to ₹7.5 lakh in 2009, and to ₹25 lahks in 2020.

 
 
• 
 
Thus, the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna (Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award) Award is the** highest sports award for any sportsperson in India**.

 
 
 
 
• **​Sharath Kamal Achanta​​** 
 
 
• Sharath Kamal is a **table tennis player from Tamil Nadu**, India.
 
• He has represented India at the Olympics.
 
• He received the **Padma Shri, India's fourth-highest civilian honour, in 2019** and the Khel Ratna Award, India's greatest sporting honour, in 2022.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Dronacharya Award**

 
 
• The** Dronacharya Award** **was instituted in **1985.__
 
• These awards are given by the Government of India for Excellency in the field of sports coaching.
 
• The award is given only to the disciplines included in the events like Olympic Games, Paralympic Games, Asian Games, Commonwealth Games, World Championship, and World Cup along with Cricket, Indigenous Games, and Parasports.**​**
 
• **​**Dinesh Jawahar Lad has earned a niche in the world of willow and wickets by bagging the Dronacharya award this year for grooming many young cricketers, including heavyweights like Rohit Sharma and Shardul Thakur.
 
• The Dronacharya Award in the lifetime category for his contributions: **Dinesh Jawahar Lad (Cricket), Bimal Prafulla Ghosh (Football), and Raj Singh (Wrestling)**.
 
• The Dronacharya Award for outstanding coaches in the Sports and Games Regular category went to Jiwanjot Singh Teja in Archery and Mohammad Ali Qamar in Boxing.
 
• The same award also went to Suma Siddharth Shirur (Para Shooting) and Sujeet Maan (Wrestling).**Shri Raj Singh****​**

questions.question: Who among the following returned his/her medal of Kaisar-i-Hind in 1920?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Mahatma Gandhi**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• In **1920**, Mahatma Gandhi** returned the prestigious Kaisar-i-Hind medal** and two war medals to the British.
 
• Mohandas Gandhi was awarded the **Kaisar-i-Hind in 1915 by The Lord Hardinge of Penshurst** for his contribution to ambulance services **in South Africa.​**
 
• He did so as part of his support for the Khilafat movement, stating that he could not wear them "with an easy conscience" while his Muslim countrymen labored under a "wrong done to their religious sentiment".
 
• Gandhi's decision to return the medal was a powerful symbolic act in solidarity with the Khilafat cause.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **S Subramania lyer**__

 
 
• S. Subramania Iyer, also known as Sir Subbier Subramania Iyer, was a distinguished Indian lawyer, jurist, and freedom fighter.
 
• Subramania Iyer advocated for tenant protection against arbitrary eviction by landlords before the Famine Commission in 1877.
 
• Judicial Career:
 
• He was the **first Indian Chief Justice of the Madras High Court**.
 
• Freedom Fighter and Home Rule Movement:
 
• Alongside Annie Besant, he co-founded the Home Rule Movement.
 
• He is also known as the **"Grand Old Man of South India."**

questions.question: Raja and Radha Reddy received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for their contribution to ______ dance.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Kuchipudi**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• Raja and Radha Reddy, the celebrated Kuchipudi dancing couple, were honored with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for their significant **contribution to the art form**.
 
• The Kuchipudi dancing pair got official recognition by winning the **Padma Shree award in 1984.**
 
• They won the prestigious Sangeet Nataka Academy Award on** 18th February 1992.**
 
• hey have individually bagged the **Padma Bhushan Award in January 2000.​​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• Kuchipudi, one of the eight prominent Indian classical dance forms, **originates** from the village of Kuchipudi in the state of **Andhra Pradesh**, India. 
 
• It is a** dance-drama performance** deeply rooted in the ancient Hindu Sanskrit text Natya Shastra. 
 
• Like other classical dances of India, Kuchipudi evolved as a religious art associated with itinerant storytellers, temples, and spiritual traditions. Originally, Kuchipudi was exclusively **performed by all-male troupes**. 
 
• In traditional performances, male dancers would portray female roles while adorned in** Agnivastra**, also known as** Bagalbandi**, and wearing a dhoti, a single pleated garment draped around the waist.

questions.question: Kumudini Lakhia is an exponent of which Indian classical dance form?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Kathak**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• Kumudini Lakhia, born on May 17, 1930, is an famous Indian Kathak dancer and choreographer based in Ahmedabad, Gujarat.
 
• She played a crucial role in reshaping the **traditional solo form of Kathak**, especially during the 1960s.
 
• Her famous choreographies include** "Dhabkar", "Yugal", and "Atah Kim"**.
 
• She also contributed as a choreographer in the Hindi film** "Umrao Jaan" (1981).​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• ​The **National Institute of Kathak Dance** is located in** New Delhi,** India.
 
• ​It **originated **in the northern part of India and has its roots in the **Mughal era**.
 
• The institute was established in** 1980** by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, an autonomous organization under the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, to promote and preserve the classical dance form of Kathak.
 
• Kathak dance is one of the** eight classical dance** forms of India and is known for its intricate footwork, graceful movements, and storytelling through dance.

questions.question: On which day of the Hindu calendar is the festival of Holi celebrated?
questions.solution:
correct answer is__** Falgun Poornima.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the Hindu calendar, Holi is celebrated every year on the **full moon day of the month of Falgun.**
 
• Hindu mythology serves as the inspiration for the vibrant and colourful festival of Holi.
 
• It is thought to derive from the **story of Hiranyakashipu and Prahlad**.
 
• It is said that **Lord Vishnu saved** his** devoted disciple Prahlad **from the nefarious plans of **his father Hiranyakashyap.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• ​Also known as **Festival of colours**, in **West Bengal, Assam and Tripura,** it is also known as the **'Dol jatra' or 'Basanta Utsav'.**​
 
• Symbolising the** triumph of good over evil **celebrated on Holika Dahan, the first day of Holi.
 
• This festival spans **two consecutive days,** beginning with **Choti Holi followed by Dulhendi**, also known as Badi Holi or Rang wali Holi.
 
• On the eve of **Choti Holi,** **Holika Dahan**, a symbolic bonfire, is ceremoniously lit.
 
• **Water and colours** are used as payment on** Dulhendi Day**.
 
• They visit each other's homes and **put gulaal, or bright colours**,** on their faces** as they joyfully celebrate this vibrant festival.

questions.question: The Taxation Laws (Amendment) Act, 2021, amends the Income Tax Act of ______.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**1961**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Taxation Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2021** was introduced in Lok Sabha by the Minister of Finance, Ms. Nirmala Sitharaman, on August 5, 2021. 
 
• The Bill **amends the Income Tax Act, 1961** (IT Act) and the** Finance Act, 2012**. 
 
• It provides that no tax demand shall be raised in the future based on the amendment to section 9 of the Income Tax Act (made via the Finance Act, 2012) for any offshore indirect transfer of Indian assets if the transaction occurred before May 28, 2012.
 
• The Act also specifies that the demand raised for offshore indirect transfer of Indian assets would be nullified upon fulfilling specified conditions, including the withdrawal of pending litigation and an undertaking not to file damage claims.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****__Timeline of Events:__**

 
• August 5, 2021: Bill introduced in the Lok Sabha.
 
• August 6, 2021: Passed in the Lok Sabha.
 
• August 9, 2021: The Rajya Sabha approved the Bill.
 
• August 13, 2021: Received the President’s assent.

__
 
• **Nor’wester****,** also known as **Bardoli Chheerha** in some regions, is a localized weather phenomenon.

 
 
• ​Also known as **kalbaisakhi**
 
 
 
• Nor’westers occur in **Bangladesh** and several Indian states,
 
 
• Including **Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, Tripura, Assam, and West Bengal** during the summer.
 
 
 
• It brings **destruction **by uprooting trees due to **gale winds and water logging roads **from heavy rainfall.
 
• However **they are beneficial for Kharif crops** like jute and paddy,

 __
 
• Mango showers **typically occur before the official onset of the monsoon season.**
 
• They are primarily experienced in the **southern and western regions of India.**
 
• These showers **usually grace** the Indian subcontinent during **April to June.**
 
• **Farmers** consider mango showers as a **prelude to the planting season.**
 
 
 
• **Blossom Shower****​**
 
 
• Blossom showers are a **natural weather phenomenon** that occurs during the **spring season**.
 
• These showers are **characterized by **a **combination of light rain and sunshine**.
 
• **Kerala** is particularly known for its beautiful blossom showers.
 
• The flowering season in Kerala generally starts in **February** and lasts till **April**.
 
 
 
• **Loo**____**​**__
 
 
• ** Hot, dry wind over North India and Pakistan.**

questions.question: The Bahmani kingdom was founded by Alauddin Bahman Shah in ______.
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is **1347.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bahmani kingdom** was a Muslim state of the Deccan in southern India and was one of the great medieval Indian kingdoms.
 
• It was founded by **Alauddin Hasan Bahaman Shah in 1347**.
 
• It was the **first Independent **Islamic Kingdom in **South India.**
 
• His kingdom included the **whole of Deccan **up to the **river Krishna** with its capital at Gulbarga.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Deccan region was a part of the provincial administration of the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• In order to establish a stable administration in the Deccan, Mohammad bin Tughlaq appointed amiran-i-sada/ Sada Amir, who were the administrative heads of hundred villages.
 
• From 1337 the conflict between the officers in Deccan and Delhi sultanate accelerated.
 
• This led to the establishment of an independent state in the Deccan in 1347 with the capital at Gulbarga in Karnataka.
 
• Rivalry with the Vijayanagar kingdom over the fertile region of Raichur doab started during his period and continued till the last of Bahaman rule.
 
• He had frequent conflicts with the Warangal state, reddy kingdoms of Rajahmundry and Kondavidu. Bahman Shah emerged victorious in all these expeditions and assumed the title of Second Alexander on his coins.

questions.question: What is the ratio by mass of hydrogen and oxygen in water?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __**1:8.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

 
• Molar Mass: The molar mass of a substance is the mass of one mole of that substance. The molar mass of water (H2O) is **18.0153 g/mo**l.
 
• Mass Percentage: The mass percentage of an element in a compound is the mass of that element in the compound divided by the total mass of the compound, multiplied by 100%
 
• **Hydrogen****​**
 
 
• Henry Cavendish discovered hydrogen in 1766.
 
• Hydrogen was termed as the " inflammable air" by Henry Cavendish. In his paper "On Factitious Airs", he mentioned that the inflammable air formed water on combustion.
 
• The name " hydrogen" was later given by **Antoine**** **Lavoisier.

questions.question: Select the natural port of India from the following.
questions.solution:

• **Natural Harbor** occurs where land and water converge in such a way as to protect ships from wind and waves as they enter and dock.
 
• They are typically formed typically in bays, estuaries, and river mouths.
 
• **Mumbai Port**
 
 
• Mumbai is the** largest natural port** in India.
 
• It is India’s largest port by size and shipping traffic.
 
• It is located in **west Mumbai on the western coast** of India.
 
• It allows easy docking and passage for large cargo ships.
 
• It handles numerous imports and exports, including crude and petroleum oil, as well as liquid chemicals, etc.

• Tamil Nadu and Puducherry are its hinterlands.

• Kolkata Port is also confronted with the problem of silt accumulation in the Hugli river which provides a link to the sea.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India provides that there shall be a Legislative Assembly for the National Capital Territory of Delhi?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is** Article 239AA.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The status of** Delhi **being a **Union Territory under Schedule 1** of the Constitution but christened the **‘National Capital Territory’ **under **Article 239AA.**
 
• The** 69th amendment** to the Constitution of India inserted **Article 239AA**, which declared the Union Territory of Delhi to be administered by a LG who works on aid and advice of the elected legislative assembly.
 
• However, the **‘aid and advice’ **clause pertains only to matters on which the elected Assembly has powers under the **State and Concurrent Lists** with the exception of **public order, police, and land.**
 
• Further, the** Article 239AA **also notes that LG has to either act on the aid and advice of the **Council of Ministers**, or he is bound to implement the decision taken by the President on a reference being made by him.
 
• Also, **Article 239AA**, empowers the LG to refer a difference of opinion on ‘any matter’ with the Council of Ministers to the President.
 
• Thus, this dual control between LG and the elected government leads to a power tussle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **National Capital Region (NCR) **is a planning region centred upon the National Capital Territory (NCT) of Delhi in India.
 
• It encompasses Delhi and several districts surrounding it from the states of Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, and Rajasthan.
 
• Delhi is of great historical significance as an important commercial, transport, and cultural hub, as well as the political centre of India.
 
• According to legend, the city was named for Raja Dhilu, a king who reigned in the region in the 1st century BC.
